title: Cathode-ray receivers · 3

techniques.name: Product line drawing
techniques.implementation: A television drawn front-on in one ink at two weights, main 1.5 px and fine 1 px, with no fill; secondary lines are the same ink at lower opacity. Drawn here by code from the sheet’s own numbers.

techniques.name: Cabinet

corner.label: Corner radius
corner.note: How round the cabinet’s corners are, as a share of its height; the mask and tube follow.

prop.label: Proportion
prop.note: Cabinet width as a multiple of its height; the tube takes the change, the controls stay put.

handle.label: Handle
handle.note: The carrying loop over the top of the cabinet.

antenna.label: Antenna
antenna.note: What stands on top, right of the handle: nothing (the sheet’s), a whip, or rabbit ears.

techniques.limits: corner radius stops at 14% of the height: the set is fully rounded there, and further the rounding would crowd the controls. Proportion stays where the tube runs between square and about 1.5 : 1 and the column keeps its width.
techniques.implementation: A rounded rectangle with quadratic corners in the main line; rails, handle, feet and antenna are laid from its edges, so they keep their places as the corner and the width change. The mask and tube corners follow the cabinet’s, concentric, once it outgrows them; the sheet’s is 10 px on a 330 px cabinet (3%). Proportion: the tube and its mask take the change in width; the column of controls and the handle’s arms keep their places. Antenna: None is the sheet’s; Whip is the CUBE’s telescopic mast with its phantom extension; Rabbit ears are two masts from a dome. Both stand at the right, clear of the handle.

techniques.name: Tube

bulge.label: Bulge
bulge.note: How far each edge of the tube face bows out; 0 is a flat rectangle.

glass.label: Glass lines
glass.note: Faint lines at the top and bottom of the face; 0 is clear glass.

picture.label: Picture
picture.note: Raster lights the set with dashed scan lines, as the sheet’s PVM does.

techniques.limits: bulge stops at 12%: past it the face reads as a cushion, not a tube. Glass lines stop at 5 per edge, before they reach the middle of the face.
techniques.implementation: The mask is a rounded rectangle in fine line; the face is four quadratic edges bowed out by the bulge, with rounded corners. Glass lines sit at the sheet’s fractions of the half-height (0.965, 0.885, 0.77), extended by the same power law (1 − 0.035·k^1.715), each inset to clear the corner.

techniques.name: Controls

fit.label: Control set
fit.note: Two tuner Dials (the sheet’s), three Knobs, or five push Buttons.

grille.label: Grille
grille.note: The speaker grille under the controls: Slots (the sheet’s), a Dots checkerboard, or None.

techniques.limits: each control set uses the sheet’s own parts and spacing, laid in the same place, so none is scaled to squeeze in.
techniques.implementation: Control sets, in the column beside the tube. Dials: two tuner dials, the sheet’s. Knobs: three pointer knobs. Buttons: five push buttons in a stack, as on the POCKET. Dials are a main-line circle with a cap at 0.32 of the radius and twelve ticks; knobs a fine circle with a pointer from 0.35 of the radius; buttons small rounded rectangles; grilles fine slots at 0.6 or a checkerboard of dots.

techniques.name: Line

weight.label: Line weight
weight.note: Fine-line width in the sheet’s px (main lines are 1.5 times it); 1 is the sheet’s hairline.

hand.label: Hand
hand.note: How far the drawing wanders from ruled, in the sheet’s px; 0 is ruled.

seed.label: Deal
seed.note: Turns the knobs to new settings and deals a new hand; No. 1 is the sheet’s.

techniques.limits: line weight stops at 0.7 px, where the fine lines would fade into the ground, and at 2 px, where knobs start to fill in. Hand stops at 1 px, past which the set reads as warped rather than drawn.
techniques.implementation: Every part is flattened to a polyline, then stroked in one ink with round caps and joins. Hand moves every point of the drawing through one smooth seeded field (two octaves, 70 and 22 px), so lines bow as if drawn freehand while joints stay joined and small circles stay round.

techniques.name: Measured inks
techniques.implementation: solid ink pixels of each figure, read at full resolution, are clustered to five colors; a color is kept when it holds at least 4% of the ink.

techniques.name: Figure and ground
techniques.implementation: The ground is the most common border color of a figure; ink is every pixel more than 40 levels from it.
